findings.finding: ISS-001 (limitation/jurisdiction) has been left undecided through Hearings 1-4 - correctly, at each of those case-management-testing stages, because deciding a threshold jurisdictional question on an admittedly assumed foundation would itself have been unsafe. It cannot be left undecided at this, the final hearing: there is no Hearing 6, and a full-merits Tribunal that declines to rule on whether it has jurisdiction has not actually decided the case. The claimant carries the legal burden of proving in-time presentation (ERA 1996 s.111(2)(a), independently verified live against legislation.gov.uk per procedure/limitation.md). On the record actually before this Tribunal: the EDT is ASSUMED, not documented (F-002); the ACAS EC certificate date (Day B) is likewise ASSUMED (F-003); the ACAS EC contact date (Day A), without which the ERA 1996 s.207B calculation cannot be run at all, is UNKNOWN (F-004); and - a distinct and more basic gap first identified at Hearing 4 - the actual date the ET1 was, or will be, presented is not stated anywhere in this matter's record at all. A Tribunal cannot find in-time presentation proved when it cannot even confirm presentation occurred. This burden has not been discharged.

In the alternative, and independently of the jurisdictional finding: ISS-002 (ordinary unfair dismissal) fails on its own terms because continuity of employment under ERA 1996 s.108 (F-008) remains completely unproven - no contract, statement of terms, or HR service record exists in this record, and the claimant's own case theory (final/case_theory_memo.md Section 3) itself runs this head only as a contingent fallback for exactly this reason. An evidential burden that has never been engaged with any document cannot be found discharged.

ISS-003 (s.103A automatic unfair dismissal) and ISS-004 (s.47B whistleblowing detriment) - the claimant's own correctly-chosen lead heads, resting on sound and binding doctrine (Kuzel v Roche Products [2008] EWCA Civ 380; Beatt v Croydon Health Services NHS Trust [2017] EWCA Civ 401; NHS Manchester v Fecitt [2011] EWCA Civ 1190, now correctly corrected for ERA 1996 s.47B(1A)-(1E)) - fail on this record for want of anything to apply that doctrine to. Kuzel requires the claimant to adduce 'some evidence' that the disclosure was the reason (or a ground) for the treatment; that exercise cannot be performed where the disclosure's own content, recipient, and date (F-010) and its sequencing against the disciplinary process (F-012) are both unstated, and where the Respondent's actual stated reason for dismissal (F-020) has never been produced. No Evidence Ledger exists anywhere in this matter (confirmed again this session: no evidence/ directory, no schemas/evidence.schema.json record). Two closing submissions that both correctly state the same doctrine and both candidly concede the same missing facts are advocacy about a case, not a demonstration of one.

A further, independent obstacle to ISS-003/ISS-004, raised for the first time in this matter's live record by the opposing case and not answered by any reply: ERA 1996 s.43B(1), as amended by Enterprise and Regulatory Reform Act 2013 s.17 (reversing Parkins v Sodexho Ltd [2002] IRLR 109), requires the worker to hold a reasonable belief that the disclosure was made in the public interest, per Chesterton Global Ltd v Nurmohamed [2017] EWCA Civ 979. The claimant's own case theory (final/case_theory_memo.md Section 3 and Section 7) declines to engage this test at all, on the stated ground that Chesterton is not yet logged in authorities.json - a defensible authority-integrity position, but one that leaves the point standing entirely unrebutted before this Tribunal. Since F-010 discloses nothing about the disclosure's content, this Tribunal cannot find, on this record, that the public-interest element is met even provisionally. This compounds the causation gap in the finding above; it does not merely repeat it.

ISS-009 (procedural fairness/remedy: Polkey deduction, ACAS Code uplift) does not arise, because no liability head survives to reach it. Independently, and as found at Hearings 3-4, it would in any event be unassessable: the disciplinary process file and the Respondent's stated reason for dismissal (F-020) have never been produced, so neither a Polkey percentage nor an ACAS Code compliance finding can be made even hypothetically.

ISS-005 (disability status, gateway), ISS-006 (discrimination arising from disability), ISS-007 (reasonable adjustments), and ISS-008 (victimisation) remain struck from Hearing 1, on a pleading defect never cured across five hearings: no impairment is named (F-021), no PCP is identified (F-024), and no protected act under Equality Act 2010 s.27(2) is identified (F-023). The claimant's own case theory (final/case_theory_memo.md Section 4) does not attempt to revive them and expressly agrees Hearing 1's strike was correctly reasoned, not merely correctly ordered. The opposing case (Part B.4) likewise does not attempt to defeat them on any ground beyond the same pleading gap, and candidly names a real risk to the Respondent (Gallop v Newport City Council) that would apply if they were ever properly pleaded. Neither side asks this Tribunal to revisit the strike, and it is not revisited.

Authority-integrity finding, carried forward and now unmet for a fourth consecutive hearing: British Home Stores Ltd v Burchell, Iceland Frozen Foods Ltd v Jones, Polkey v A E Dayton Services Ltd, Chesterton Global Ltd v Nurmohamed, J v DLA Piper UK LLP, and the ERRA 2013 s.17 amendment - all relied on in the opposing case, and Chesterton specifically outcome-relevant to the finding above - remain absent from authorities.json, which independently re-read this session still runs only to AUTH-007. This does not change today's disposition, because the underlying propositions are treated as correctly stated general doctrine (none is doubted as fabricated, and the opposing case's own verification narrative for all six is candid about tier and sources), but a five-hearing run that never once cures a repair first ordered at Hearing 2 is itself a finding about this matter's own record-keeping, not only about the parties' cases.

The Respondent's identity (F-025) remains unconfirmed - directed at every prior hearing, still not addressed by either side at the final hearing. A claim cannot proceed to a judgment capable of enforcement against an unidentified party; this is a freestanding pleading defect, not a mere restatement of the jurisdictional finding.

disposition:
Hearing 5 (FULL_MERITS), M1-KESTREL, England & Wales Employment Tribunal. This Tribunal reads and builds on the real Hearing 1-4 records supplied to it, and on the real final/case_theory_memo.md and opposition/opposition_case.md that now actually exist in the workspace - not on the stale matters/M1-KESTREL/moot/hearing-5.json already on disk, which cited a 'Hearing 2' and cited five (not six) opposition authorities in a form that predates the real documents this Tribunal has actually been given. This record supersedes that stale hearing-5.json in full; its substantive conclusion happens to converge with this Tribunal's own independently-reasoned conclusion in significant part, which is the real record speaking twice, not deference to an unauthenticated prior transcript.

The claim, as it presently stands and on the record actually before this Tribunal, is dismissed. Primary and independently sufficient basis: the claimant has not discharged the burden of showing this Tribunal has jurisdiction to hear any complaint in this matter (ISS-001). The effective date of termination is assumed, not documented; the ACAS EC certificate date is assumed; the ACAS EC contact date required to run the ERA 1996 s.207B calculation is unknown outright; and - more fundamentally still - no date, or confirmation, of the ET1's actual presentation appears anywhere in this matter's record. A Tribunal cannot find a claim to have been presented in time when it cannot confirm the claim was presented at all.

In the alternative, and independently: even assuming jurisdiction were established, every surviving substantive head fails for want of proof. ISS-002 fails because continuity of employment (F-008) is wholly unproven, a gap the claimant's own case theory concedes by running that head only as a contingent fallback. ISS-003 and ISS-004 - correctly identified by the claimant as the strongest available heads, and resting on sound, binding, correctly-stated authority (Kuzel, Beatt, and Fecitt as properly corrected for the ERRA 2013 co-worker amendment) - fail because the protected disclosure's content, recipient, date, and sequencing against the disciplinary process, and the Respondent's actual stated reason for dismissal, have never been produced in any form; no Evidence Ledger has ever existed in this matter. A further and independent obstacle to ISS-003/ISS-004, raised by the opposing case and never answered: the ERA 1996 s.43B(1)/Chesterton public-interest requirement cannot be assessed, let alone found met, where the disclosure's content is entirely unknown - the claimant's own case theory declines to engage this test at all, leaving it unrebutted. ISS-009 does not arise, no liability head having survived to reach it, and would in any event be unassessable for want of the disciplinary file. ISS-005 to ISS-008 remain struck from Hearing 1 on an uncured pleading defect and are not revived; neither side asked this Tribunal to revisit that strike.

The six-authority logging repair directed at Hearing 2 remains unmet for a fourth consecutive hearing. The Respondent's identity (F-025) remains unconfirmed. Neither defect changes today's outcome, but both are recorded as uncured across the entire five-hearing run. This disposition is without prejudice to a fresh claim or application supported by the actual documents this matter has sought, and failed to obtain, since Hearing 1: the termination letter, the ACAS EC certificate itself, confirmation of the ET1's presentation, the disciplinary file, the protected disclosure(s), and the contradictory emails.
reasons:
I read workflows/five-hearing-adversarial.md, agents/judiciary/ROLE.md, schemas/hearing.schema.json, and every file in matters/M1-KESTREL/ - facts/facts.json, issues/issues.json, authorities/authorities.json (independently re-read and confirmed it still runs only to AUTH-007), chronology/chronology.json, chronology/chronology_gaps.md, procedure/limitation.md, intake/matter.json, the real final/case_theory_memo.md and opposition/opposition_case.md supplied for this hearing, and the full real Hearing 1-4 records supplied in the prompt. I also read the stale moot/hearing-5.json already on disk before overwriting it, precisely so I could check rather than assume it rested on the same broken evidentiary chain Hearing 1 identified for the earlier stale hearing-3/4/5.json files: it does (its 'authority-integrity' finding names 'five further authorities' and attributes the direction to log them to 'Hearings 2, 3 and 4' collectively, without independently distinguishing what the real Hearing 2 record - now actually available to me - in fact ordered, and without engaging the sixth authority, the ERRA 2013 s.17 amendment itself, or the specific Chesterton public-interest point the real opposition_case.md raises). I did not treat its findings as settled prior authority for that reason, even though my own independent reading reaches substantially the same disposition on jurisdiction and on the evidential vacuum - that convergence is this hearing's own reasoning speaking for itself, not adoption of an unauthenticated transcript.

A full-merits hearing is the point at which a decision-maker must actually decide, not defer again, applying agents/judiciary/ROLE.md's instruction not to avoid an actual disposition. On jurisdiction, I gave the same weight to burden allocation that every one of my Read/Grep/Glob-only tool contract's fellow hearings has given it throughout this matter: the burden of proving in-time presentation has always sat with the claimant, and I cannot responsibly find it discharged on an assumed EDT, an unknown Day A, and - the more basic gap Hearing 4 first surfaced and which I independently re-confirmed is still true today by re-reading facts.json and issues.json - no confirmation anywhere in this record that an ET1 has ever actually been presented. I gave this as the primary, independently sufficient basis for dismissal, then gave a full alternative merits analysis rather than resting on jurisdiction alone, consistent with the stale prior hearing-5.json's own reasoning that a Tribunal deciding against a party on a threshold point without also testing the substance invites exactly the unexamined outcome this workflow exists to prevent - I adopt that methodological point on its own merits, having verified it is sound reasoning, not because the file that stated it is authoritative.

On the merits, I did not re-decide anything Hearings 1-3 already settled: I did not revisit the ISS-005 to ISS-008 strike (neither side asked me to, and I confirmed by reading both final/case_theory_memo.md Section 4 and opposition/opposition_case.md Part B.4 in full that neither attempts to revive them), and I treated Kuzel, Beatt, and the corrected Fecitt as correctly and consistently stated doctrine, which they are - Hearing 2's doctrinal screen is not reopened here. What I did apply, independently, is the actual evidential test Hearing 3 first ran and Hearing 4 found still unrepaired: an Evidence Ledger that has never existed across five hearings cannot support a finding for the claimant on any contested element, however sound the underlying doctrine. I gave particular weight to a point genuinely new to this hearing's record: the opposing case's public-interest argument under ERA 1996 s.43B(1)/ERRA 2013 s.17/Chesterton Global v Nurmohamed is raised squarely against the claimant's lead heads, and final/case_theory_memo.md's own Section 7 expressly declines to engage it at all (citing the authority's unlogged status in authorities.json) rather than meeting it on its substance. I treated that as a real, independent, currently-unrebutted obstacle to ISS-003/ISS-004 - not merely a repeat of the causation-evidence gap - because a disclosure whose content is entirely unknown cannot be shown to meet a test that turns specifically on the content and effect of the disclosure. I likewise noted, without it affecting today's outcome, the opposing case's candidly two-edged points (that limitation on this record shows only unproven timeliness, not actual lateness; that Gallop remains a genuine risk to the Respondent if the disability cluster is ever properly pleaded; and the conditional co-worker 'all reasonable steps' defence under ERA 1996 s.47B(1A)-(1E), which cuts for the Respondent only if the contradictory emails at F-013 turn out to be an individual's unauthorised act, a fact this record does not establish either way) - these are recorded as honest, unresolved legal questions, not as findings for either side, since ISS-004 fails independently for want of evidence regardless of how that conditional defence would eventually apply.

On authority integrity, I independently re-read authorities.json rather than trusting the stale prior hearing-5.json's characterisation of it, and confirmed the Hearing 2 logging repair - now covering six authorities, not five, once the ERRA 2013 s.17 amendment is counted alongside Burchell, Iceland Frozen Foods, Polkey, Chesterton, and J v DLA Piper - remains completely unmet for a fourth consecutive hearing. I did not treat this as doubting any of the six authorities' genuineness (the opposing case's own verification narrative is candid, multi-sourced, and consistent with this matter's existing secondary-source tier), only as unlogged in the matter's own ledger, exactly as Hearings 2 and 3 reasoned. I added no entry to authorities.json myself, consistent with this matter's established practice that the ledger is maintained by the solicitors/opposition roles, not by this Tribunal, and I relied on no authority not already logged there or presented with a documented verification trail by a party. My statements on Polkey's continuing procedural relevance and on the general availability of reinstatement/uncapped compensation for s.103A/s.47B claims are consistent with, and do not extend beyond, what this matter's own prior hearings and the parties' filed documents have already stated - I did not independently re-verify any remedy statute this session beyond what is already logged, and none of it is outcome-determinative given that no liability head survives to reach remedy.
concessions_made: Both closing submissions were candid, not evasive, about the evidentiary gap: the claimant's own case theory again declines to assert disability, disclosure content, causation sequencing, the Respondent's stated reason, or a specific protected act as established, and expressly agrees Hearing 1's strike of ISS-005 to ISS-008 was correctly reasoned rather than merely correctly ordered. The opposing case likewise does not manufacture disagreement with that concession, or invent an unfavourable fact against the claimant beyond what the record actually shows, and names a genuine risk to the Respondent (Gallop) rather than omitting it.

The doctrinal statement of Fecitt (as corrected for ERRA 2013), Kuzel, and Beatt remains correctly described by both sides; today's disposition is entirely evidential and, on one further point, doctrinal-but-unrebutted (the public-interest test), not a reopening of Hearing 2's doctrinal findings.
Neither side attempted to revive ISS-005 to ISS-008, correctly treating Hearing 1's strike as settled through to the final hearing.

The opposing case's account of the limitation position is honest rather than overstated: on the claimant's own worst-case assumed arithmetic, today's date still falls inside the primary three-month period, so the correct characterisation of the limitation defect is unproven timeliness, not demonstrated lateness - this Tribunal adopts that framing rather than the more aggressive version a Respondent could have overclaimed.

The seeded fabricated authority (Whitfield v Anglia NHS Foundation Trust) was independently re-checked and correctly rejected again by both real case documents this round and needs no further attention.

hot_bench_questions.question: Setting aside every other gap: is there anything anywhere in this matter's record confirming an ET1 was ever actually presented, on any date?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: No. facts.json and issues.json (ISS-001, evidence_missing) both confirm this; neither final/case_theory_memo.md nor opposition/opposition_case.md supplies a presentation date. This alone is sufficient to dispose of the matter.

hot_bench_questions.question: The claimant's own case theory concedes the s.43B(1)/Chesterton public-interest test is squarely raised against it and declines to engage it because the authority is unlogged. Is declining to engage the governing legal test a sustainable litigation position at a full-merits hearing, however defensible it is as an authority-integrity stance?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: No - authority-integrity discipline explains why the claimant will not cite Chesterton by name, but it does not excuse engaging with the underlying statutory test itself (ERA 1996 s.43B(1) as amended), which the claimant could and should have addressed on its own terms regardless of whether the case law describing it is yet logged. The point stands unrebutted.

hot_bench_questions.question: If every liability head had in fact been proved today, what would this Tribunal actually be able to award, given that ERA 1996 s.124(1A) and the availability of injury-to-feelings for a s.49 detriment claim are both flagged UNVERIFIED in this matter's own record?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: The question does not need to be answered to dispose of this hearing, since no liability head survives to remedy - but it is recorded that this matter's remedy analysis would itself need independent primary-source verification before any award could safely be quantified, a gap that has existed since Hearing 4 and remains unclosed.

residual_uncertainty: This is a simulated hearing decided on a closed hypothetical record that was never supplemented with a single primary document, witness statement, or piece of disclosure across five hearings - not an actual trial. A real tribunal presented with the termination letter, the ACAS EC certificate, confirmation of the ET1's actual presentation date, the disciplinary file, the protected disclosure(s) themselves, the OH material, and the contradictory emails could reach a materially different result on both jurisdiction and every substantive head - this disposition is bound only by the record actually and consistently maintained through this matter's five hearings, and is not a finding that the underlying facts, once produced, would not sustain the claim. Separately, and outside this Tribunal's own jurisdiction to resolve: the workflow's own procedural gap (it does not model the interim case-management layer - strike-out applications, unless orders, disclosure directions - that a real matter in this state would have passed through long before any full-merits hearing could be listed) means this hearing has, by necessity, tested a case at a full-merits stage that a real Employment Tribunal would very likely never have allowed to reach that stage without those primary documents first. That is a limitation of the simulation, not a finding about this matter's underlying merits.
